steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine flour and 1/3 cup brown sugar in a mixer. Mix in softened butter until a dough has formed. Press into an ungreased 8x8-inch baking pan; prick dough with a fork.
Bake shortbread in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, beat egg in a mixing bowl along with 1/3 cup brown sugar, maple syrup, and pecans. Pour pecan mixture over hot crust, and return to oven. Continue baking until topping has firmed, 12 to 15 minutes.
Remove from oven, and immediately run a knife around the edges to prevent sticking. Cool completely, then cut into 1-inch bar cookies to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Maple Pecan Shortbread Squares
raw_recipe.description: Real maple syrup flavors the sticky pecan topping of these delicious shortbread squares.

video.description: Turn the classic pecan pie on its head and serve up these delicious butter shortbread crusted bars filled with gooey maple syrup and crunchy pecans. Best of all this recipe is super simple, so you’ll be on your way to the ultimate in rich dessert satisfaction in no time. Mix flour with brown sugar and softened butter and press into a baking dish. While you bake this decadent shortbread, create the rich filling by mixing an egg with brown sugar, maple syrup and chopped pecans. Pour this mixture over the hot crust when it’s fresh from the oven and bake further until firm, then cut into squares or diamonds when cool. Then give into all the elements you love: sweet maple, rich caramel nutty crunch, all delivered on a tender butter cookie. Yum!

review.reviewBody: These are absolutely delicious bars! The amount of pecans is perfect, the filling was just slightly gooey, and the shortbread base is so buttery and delicious. The only thing wrong with these is that the maple flavor isn't all that present...you can taste a delightful hint of it in the bars, but they aren't extremely maple-y. I may decide to add some maple flavoring to the next batch I make, because adding more syrup would mess too much with the texture of the filling. I lined my baking pan with Reynold's release foil so that I could just take the whole section of cooled bars right out of the pan for ease of cutting. I did cut them into triangles instead of one inch squares...I thought they looked prettier that way. Thanks so much for sharing this recipe...it's a winner!

Excellent! Here are my additions: 1). doubled batch; 2). used 1/3 brown and 1/3 white sugar in the dough; 3). added 1/3 c. shredded coconut and 1/2 tsp. cinnamon to the topping; 4). lined the pan with foil and lightly coated with Wilson's Cake Release; 5). Immediately after removing from oven I sprinked lightly and evenly with miniature semi-sweet chocolate chips (don't spread when they melt - just let them 'dot' the cookies with little bursts of chocolate).

After cooling almost completely; the bars cut beautifully!

For first time shortbread makers - let the butter come to room temperature naturally - don't try to microwave it. Then cut the sticks into little cubes, and sprinkle the cubes into the flour/sugar mixture as you're mixing it. Mix on low to medium speed and don't overmix. Taking this extra care with the butter and using a standing mixer will make a beautiful dough that is evenly incorporated, allowing you to just lift the dough out and press right into the pan.

AMAZING!
I am going to make these again for sure!
The only thing i changed was the pan i used. I didnt have an 8x8 so i used my cupcake trays. this recipe makes 12 cupcakes size discs. they were a perfect 2 bites and best of all i used cupcake liners so i had no clean up. unwrap and serve they looked nice and neat. In future i will make 2 trays worth. If i do that i would double the shortbread crust and triple the filling. I found the crust was perfect for 12 cupcake size bites but i could have used a bit more filling. Seriously good. You have to try this easy and addicting treat!

Great taste. Super simple to make. I added a pinch of salt to the dough and used pecan halves (though chopped pecans might have made it easier to cut). I lined the pan with parchment paper to make them easy to remove.

I used sucanat in place of the brown sugar. It has a slight molasses undertone. I let the maple syrup dissolve the(second half of) sucanat for about 10 minutes before adding the egg and pecans. I doubled the amount of pecans. After adding the pecan mixture to the crust, I baked a little longer, 15-16 minutes, due to the extra pecans. I liked this very much. I am making these to pass out to neighbors for the holidays, along with some home made dog treats, also from this site.

These were a big hit at work! The recipe turns out perfectly as written.(I did add a pinch of salt though.) They even came out of the glass baking dish quite easily. The 2nd time I made them I added a tablespoon of bourbon to the pecan & maple filling and toasted the pecans as I would with a pecan pie. It adds another depth of flavor that I really like.

Giving this 5 stars because even the people who don't normally eat dessert enjoyed this. Easier then pecan pie. I used salted butter in the shortbread. I toasted my pecans and used about a cup. I added a quarter tsp of bourbon to the pecan mixture. I take recipes as a starting point - oven temp and humidity have a definite impact. I cooked my shortbread until it smelled done. I also used an electric mixer on the egg/sugar/syrup combo and got it nice and thick and frothy. If you don't beat it long enough you will end up with a runny result. 

I used buttered parchment paper on the bottom of the pan - didn't even trim it. I did poke a generous amount of holes in the shortbread before baking - there might have been more holes than dough.

My husband went back for 4ths.

Will definitely make again, especially since it can be eaten by hand, unlike a pie.

These are delicious! I made them with gluten free flour (Bob's Red Mill 1 to 1), added about 1/4 tsp of pure vanilla extract, and increased the amount of pecans to 3/4 cup. The time for the crust varies whether or not you use a glass or metal pan (cooks faster in metal-about 3 minutes less for golden brown). Thanks for the recipe!

First and foremost, thank you Tracy for putting this recipe into print and sharing with everyone. I have been making this recipe for a very long time and get requests to make it all the time. I've been reading the reviews from other bakers and there are a few who just can't follow a recipe and so the end result is frustrating. For this recipe, I found using a glass baking dish, weather an 8x8 or a 9x13 and lightly sprayed with cooking spray, works phenomenal for not sticking. If you don't have glass bakeware, then yes, aluminum foil lightly sprayed, works like a charm. The recipe is perfect as is. Why fix something that "ain't" broke??? To answer another reader's question --I press the shortbread up the sides of the dish to hold the topping a bit better. Second, as the recipe instructs, the crust must be completely cool before pouring on the topping to bake. This prevents the base from getting soggy and sticking to the pan. Also, check the bars after 12 minutes or so to see that the edges are not too brown. The center will be a little soft and wobbly when done. Remove the pan from the oven at this point since as the bars are cooling, the heat from the pan will continue to bake the batter. Serve warm or at room temperature.
This is a great recipe! Whenever I take some to a potluck, my friends fight over it. I've also tried it with about 1/4 cup of chopped crisp bacon in addition to the pecans. YUM!

These are absolutely spectacular! I didn't imagine just how wonderful these would be! I also added 1/3 of Skor bits (the kind you get in the same place in the grocery store as chocolate chips) to the pecan mixture and they are to DIE for!!!!!

Caught this recipe- without the chopped pecans but with pecans on top- in the All Recipes magazine and had to try it. It is delicious! Didn’t last a whole 24 hours in this house. I’m going to have to make them again today.
Made exactly as written above. Tasty, but shortbread was a little soft and stuck to glass’s pan on the bottom. Would make again but with tweaks from other reviews.
Best pecan bars ever! The shortbread buttery crust is amazing and so it the topping with real maple syrup. I did add a little maple extract as some people suggested.

I decided to make something sweet for my family and wow this didn't disappoint!!! It was beyond easy and turned out so good! Highly recommend for anyone who needs an easy, fantastic dessert for a get together!
I made this exactly as written and it was delicious!! Definitely a keeper. I liked the crust because it was so tender and flaky.
I had to use walnuts,(my pecans disappeared ),followed the recipe These are unbelievable,so delicious! I will definitely make again and again, with the walnuts as well as with pecans. Thank you Beth
Made it as written. It's so good! Will be making this again.
This is the most easy and richest recipe. My go-to recipe for taking dessert to a friend.

Very easy and super delicious. I used dark brown sugar for the crust and added extra pecans. Baked it a few minutes longer because the center of the topping was still a little soft. The result is what I called “maple pecan pie bites”. My friend asked for pecan pie for a dinner party dessert and was very pleased.
